title: ICC temporal jurisdiction — event date versus legal applicability
description: Tests EVENT × LAW correlation while keeping legal applicability separate from guilt, liability, or judicial judgment.

support: Article 11 makes the timing of alleged conduct legally relevant to whether ICC temporal jurisdiction can exist.
counterevidence: Temporal fit alone does not establish territorial or personal jurisdiction, admissibility, crime elements, responsibility, or guilt.
alternative_explanations: jurisdiction may arise through a later state-party date subject to the Statute
article 12(3) acceptance may alter the jurisdictional pathway
another tribunal or domestic jurisdiction may be relevant instead
edges.notes: LAW endpoint is canonical in AWS dev. The EVENT remains intentionally hypothetical/candidate; this fixture tests applicability logic only and must never be rendered as a court finding or guilt determination.
